jobs.title: Technical Product Manager - Oracle Fusion Supply Chain Finance & Costing
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
This role is part of the IT Finance Systems team and will support design, configuration, testing, and deployment of Supply Chain Finance, Costing, and Intercompany capabilities for GE HealthCare's migration from Oracle E-Business Suite R12 to Oracle Fusion Cloud. We are looking for an experienced Oracle practitioner with strong hands-on configuration skills and multiple implementations behind them, who wants to deepen their business process expertise and grow into a senior solution role.

GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our purpose is to create a world where healthcare has no limits. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

Job Description
In this role, you will

- Support end-to-end business process design and application delivery for Oracle Fusion Cost Management, inventory accounting, and Intercompany, working across Inventory, Manufacturing, Procurement, Order Management, Receivables, Payables, General Ledger, and Subledger Accounting.
- Own configuration and setup for defined areas of Oracle Fusion Cost Management, supply chain accounting, and Intercompany, including setup documentation, prototyping, and validation, and clearly explain how configuration choices affect process execution, accounting, controls, integrations, and reporting.
- Work with Finance and business stakeholders to document current-state and future-state processes for standard costing, cost elements, overheads, inventory valuation, COGS, cost accounting distributions, Subledger Accounting rules for supply chain transactions, and period-end costing activities.
- Support design and validation of intercompany trade and non-trade processes, including internal material transfers, intercompany sales and purchases, transfer pricing, markups, profit in inventory, settlement, and reconciliation.
- Participate in requirements workshops, fit-gap analysis, solution confirmation, process walkthroughs, and design documentation, escalating key decisions and risks to the senior solution lead.
- Prepare functional specifications, user stories, process flows, data mappings, test scenarios, and acceptance criteria for reports, interfaces, conversions, and extensions.
- Collaborate with technical teams to clarify functional flows, accounting logic, mappings, validation rules, reconciliation requirements, and error-handling expectations for RICE components.
- Execute and coordinate CRP, SIT, UAT, regression, conversion, and cutover testing; document defects, validate fixes, and confirm traceability to business requirements.
- Support R12-to-Fusion data migration and reconciliation, including master data, standard costs, inventory balances, open transactions, intercompany balances, and relevant accounting outputs.
- Contribute to user training, deployment readiness, hypercare, operational documentation, and continuous improvement of the global solution.
- Work alongside senior architects to build depth in cost accounting and intercompany processes and take on increasing design ownership over time.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Supply Chain, Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
- 5+ years of Finance or Supply Chain systems experience with hands-on Oracle ERP (R12 and/or Fusion) implementation experience.
- Participation in at least two full-cycle Oracle ERP implementations, with hands-on ownership of application configuration.
- Strong hands-on configuration skills in Oracle Fusion Cost Management (for example cost organizations, cost books, cost elements, cost accounting rules, standard cost setup, and cost accounting distributions) or in Inventory, Manufacturing, or Procurement accounting and Subledger Accounting, or the equivalent in Oracle E-Business Suite R12.
- Working knowledge of Oracle Fusion Intercompany and the integration of intercompany transactions with AR, AP, Inventory, Costing, and GL.
- Ability to perform application configuration and assess the downstream process and accounting impact of setup changes.
- Experience preparing functional documentation and partnering with technical teams on reports, interfaces, conversions, integrations, or extensions.
- Hands-on experience in testing, defect resolution, data validation, reconciliation, and deployment support.

Preferred / Added Advantage

- Understanding of cost accounting and intercompany processes beyond system setup, such as standard costing, overheads, inventory valuation, COGS, transfer pricing, and period-end processes.
- Exposure to an R12-to-Oracle Fusion migration or cloud ERP transformation.
- Experience in a global manufacturing, healthcare, or other complex product-based organization.
- Knowledge of OTBI, BI Publisher, FBDI, web services, and light SQL for validation and troubleshooting.
- Exposure to Oracle EPM, tax engines, reconciliation tools, or middleware platforms.
- Oracle Cloud certification or a professional accounting or finance certification.

Desired Characteristics

- Eagerness to deepen business process expertise and grow into a senior solution role.
- Strong business acumen and the ability to translate finance requirements into scalable application solutions.
- Structured problem-solving, attention to detail, and the ability to assess downstream process and system impacts.
- Strong communication and collaboration skills across Finance, Business, Product, Architecture, Development, and external implementation partners.
- A continuous-improvement mindset with a focus on standardization, controls, adoption, and sustainable support.

- Manage the full product lifecycle, including current and future versions, integrations, and feature evolution

jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
The Advanced Technical Leader leads projects and initiatives with broad scope and high impact to the business or is a recognized expert in a specialized field. The Technical Program Manager, Software Modernization & AI Enablement drives execution of the software organization’s long-term technical health — modularization, tech debt reduction, tooling, and release governance — partnering closely with architects to turn technical direction into concrete, resourced programs.

This position also leads the organization’s Generative AI enablement effort, driving adoption of AI-powered tools and workflows across all the software development poles. The Software leads own delivery of individual programs (schedule, dependencies, releases); this role owns the standards, tooling, and structural roadmap that all programs run on and improve against over time. The role operates within a regulated medical device software environment and partners closely with Quality and Regulatory functions to ensure process rigor is maintained as the organization modernizes.

Job Description
Roles and Responsibilities
- Technical Strategy Execution (Modernization)
- Partner with architects to translate technology direction (modularization, platform consolidation, tech debt reduction) into a structured, resourced program with milestones and owners.

- Own the long-term technical roadmap independent of feature/release cycles — the work that competes for attention against feature delivery.

- Build and maintain visibility into tech debt: inventory it, prioritize it with architects and software leads, and track burn-down over time.

- Identify where architectural intent isn’t translating into practice, and course-correct through structured execution rather than direct authority.

- Tooling & Process Ownership
- Own the organization’s software development tooling strategy (ALM, CI/CD, code review, defect tracking), ensuring consistency and fitness-for-purpose across all four regions.

- Evaluate, select, and roll out tooling changes with minimal disruption to active programs.

- Own core software development process definitions and drive their consistent, low-friction application across regions.

- Release Governance & Verification Readiness
- Own global standardization of the merge and release process, including Merge Committee structure, cadence, and decision rights.

- Define and maintain release governance: what needs sign-off, by whom, and at what stage, balancing rigor with delivery speed.

- Monitor the software organization’s adherence to and outcomes from the org-wide Ready-for-Verification (RFV) process, using Software Problem Report (SPR) trends found during formal verification as a leading indicator of process health, and feed findings back into tooling, process, and modernization priorities.

- Ensure release governance is applied consistently across the four regional teams, adapting for regional constraints without fragmenting the standard.

- Generative AI Enablement
- Define and run the organization’s roadmap for adopting GenAI tools in the software lifecycle (coding assistants, code review, documentation, testing).

- Establish lightweight governance: usage guidelines, security/IP considerations, and success metrics for AI tool adoption — with attention to what’s appropriate in a regulated development environment.

- Run enablement programs — training, champions network, pilot-to-scale playbooks — tailored to each region.

- Track adoption and impact (velocity, quality, satisfaction) and report ROI to leadership.

- Stay current on the GenAI tooling landscape and pressure-test new tools before wider rollout.

- Project Management & Cross-Functional Collaboration
- Act as the connective tissue between architects (who set direction), software leads (who run delivery), and regional teams (who execute) — without owning any single team’s delivery schedule.

- Partner with Quality/Regulatory to keep tooling, process, and release governance changes aligned with applicable software development lifecycle requirements (e.g., IEC 62304, design controls).

- Translate ambiguous, evolving priorities — both architectural and AI-related — into structured programs with clear owners and milestones.

Required Qualifications
- 6+ years in technical program management or a hybrid technical/execution role in a software organization; experience in a regulated industry (medical device, automotive, aerospace, or similar) strongly preferred.

- Working knowledge of formal software development lifecycle requirements (e.g., IEC 62304, design controls, V&V) and how upstream process discipline reduces downstream compliance cost.

- Experience standardizing or governing release/merge processes across multiple teams or regions.

- Strong technical fluency (C++ and MS Windows preferred) — enough to have credible, substantive conversations with architects about modularization, dependencies, and tech debt tradeoffs.

- Direct experience with, or strong working knowledge of, GenAI developer tools and how organizations adopt them, including awareness of considerations specific to regulated environments.

- Excellent stakeholder management across architects, software leads, regional teams, and Quality/Regulatory functions.

Desired Characteristics
- Prior experience leading or contributing to software modernization, platform consolidation, or tech-debt reduction initiative at organizational scale.

- Familiarity with software architecture review processes and how to translate architectural decisions into executable program plans.

- Experience with ALM/PLM tooling (e.g., Rally, ALM, DevOps) in a regulated software environment.

- Experience operating in a global, matrixed organization spanning multiple regions and time zones.

- Familiarity with GenAI governance considerations in regulated industries (data handling, IP, model output verification).
